newsitem.title: BELGIUM: European Commission escapes mad cow censure move.
newsitem.headline: European Commission escapes mad cow censure move.

text.p: The European Parliament on Thursday stepped back from censuring the European Commission over its handling of mad cow disease but deputies warned they might do so later.
A parliamentary committee of inquiry rejected an amendment by the Green Group calling for a motion of no-confidence in the Commission, the European Union's executive body.
It was one of 254 amendments to a report investigating the way the Commission had handled the 1996 mad cow crisis, which has hammered the European beef industry, and suggesting reforms.
But parliamentary sources said a fresh bid to censure the Commission could be made when the full parliament votes on the report on February 19.
"It has rejected a censure move for now, but may try again later," one source said.

The committee is calling for the creation of a public health protection unit, covering both human and animal health, independent of agricultural and industrial interests and controlled by the EU consumer affairs commissioner.
Commission President Jacques Santer told the inquiry in mid-January the Commission planned similar changes, due to be announced later this month.

The mad cow crisis erupted in March 1996 when Britain said that the cattle brain disease, bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), could be linked to a fatal human equivalent. The European Union reacted with a worldwide ban on British beef exports.
